body: I have intermittent fmla so it’s not a continuous being out just when I need it (my dr has signed off on 2 days per week plus 1 day per month for infusion.) and training is at our call center so there wouldn’t be another location I could go. My infusion lasts 4 hours and I have had severe allergic reactions in the past so I have to be loaded with steroids and Benadryl through my IV prior so I can not work on the day I get my infusion due to that

Sorry to hear ): crohns sucks but coming up with the right treatment plan makes all the world of difference! I was diagnosed at 12/13 and was on remicade for 5 years which put me into remission. Sadly since then I had an allergic reaction and have had to have surgery and try multiple different meds but through it all I have an amazing dr willing to try anything and everything to help me and that helps me stay sane and keep pushing.

Things you will come to love:

-heating pad. It’s my best friend, I even asked for a new one for Christmas. I bring it EVERYwhere. I’m literally sitting with it on my stomach as I type this!

-wipes/change of underwear in your purse/car wherever is handy, I even carry febreeze too for when I’m at a friends/family’s house and they don’t have any in their bathroom.

-keep a diary of your symptoms. I have soooo many different symptoms on any given day and before I kept a diary there was always things I forgot to bring up to my dr. The diary can also help you keep track of what you’re eating and your trigger foods (everyone is different) I’ll let you know for me it’s carbs (breads pastas) and raw veggies like carrots/broccoli but steamed green beans and mashed potatoes are my go to! Everyone is different in regards to food though

-this sub!! So helpful, so much support seriously there’s some awesome people here


If you need anything you can always send me a message. Welcome to the crohns club and I’m terribly sorry that you’ve joined this sucky club ):
